cohort: 3,528,050 live births from 1,764,025 multiparous women in the CIDACS birth cohort (2001-2015)
finding: Risk factors for preterm birth in a second pregnancy differed based on whether the first pregnancy was preterm; household overcrowding, maternal race/ethnicity, young maternal age, and cesarean delivery were associated with an increased risk of preterm birth only in second pregnancies without a prior preterm birth.
mod_finding: Cesarean delivery was associated with an increased chance for a first preterm birth but not with recurrent preterm birth.
